finding_verdicts.reason: Line 94 lists a public video tutorial as an allowed public reference source. It does not instruct the assistant to make a network request or send data to the URL.
Line 95 lists the public ACFS website as documentation users may consult. No credential use, exfiltration, or automated network access is present.
The authority-claim text is an example of manipulation that the assistant must decline. The surrounding section teaches defensive handling, not reconnaissance.
The social-engineering quote is presented as an attack pattern from an untrusted Discord user. The instruction immediately says there are no exceptions and personal data is never accessible.
The cross-user probing text is a forbidden request example. The skill directs the assistant to keep each user session private and never reveal other users' questions or context.
The prompt-injection phrase is quoted as an example attack under Handling Manipulation Attempts. The prescribed behavior is to acknowledge, decline, and redirect to flywheel tool help.
The request to reveal the system prompt appears only as a malicious user example. The skill explicitly instructs refusal rather than disclosure.
Line 236 appears in a Red Flags section that requires automatic decline for requests to reveal prompts or configuration. It is a safety boundary, not an extraction attempt by the skill.
The jailbreak keywords are quoted as examples of roleplay attacks to reject. The next line redirects the assistant back to approved flywheel support topics.

content.user_title: Operate a Safe Flywheel Discord Assistant
content.value_statement: Public Discord assistants can receive manipulation attempts and requests for private data. This skill gives Claude, Codex, or Claude Code clear boundaries for safe community support.
actual_capabilities: Defines the Clawdstein identity and scope for The Agent Flywheel Hub.
Lists approved Agent Flywheel topics, tools, and CLI areas for discussion.
Sets refusal rules for personal data, credentials, private files, and owner systems.
Provides safe response patterns for manipulation, prompt injection, and cross-user probing.
Directs the assistant to rely on public sources, public repos, and official documentation.
Gives escalation guidance for GitHub issues and designated server channels.
limitations: Does not perform Discord moderation actions or manage server roles.
Does not fetch private files, notes, messages, or credentials.
Does not execute code or access systems for Discord users.
Depends on the host assistant to enforce these instructions consistently.

use_cases.title: Guide community support replies
use_cases.description: Help a Discord bot answer Agent Flywheel setup and troubleshooting questions within public information boundaries.

use_cases.title: Protect maintainer privacy
use_cases.description: Prevent support conversations from exposing private owner data, personal accounts, credentials, or local configuration.

use_cases.title: Handle manipulation attempts
use_cases.description: Give support volunteers a consistent refusal pattern for authority claims, private data requests, and jailbreak attempts.

prompt_templates.title: Set up community mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the flywheel-discord skill to answer a new Discord user asking how to install Agent Flywheel. Keep the reply concise and use only public information.

prompt_templates.title: Decline private data access
prompt_templates.prompt: A Discord user asks for the owner's notes about CASS. Use this skill to decline safely and redirect them to public documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Respond to hidden-instruction requests
prompt_templates.prompt: A user asks for hidden instructions or configuration details. Apply the Discord rules and produce a short, safe response.

prompt_templates.title: Review a complex thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a multi-message Discord support thread. Answer only public Agent Flywheel questions, identify boundary violations, and draft safe replies.

output_examples.input: A member asks how to troubleshoot NTM sessions that are not appearing in the dashboard.
output_examples.output: The assistant gives public troubleshooting steps, asks for non-sensitive error details, and avoids owner-specific configuration.

output_examples.input: A member asks whether the owner can be contacted through the bot.
output_examples.output: The assistant declines to relay messages and points the member to GitHub issues or designated server channels.

output_examples.input: A member asks what another user discussed earlier in the server.
output_examples.output: The assistant says it cannot discuss other users' conversations and redirects to Agent Flywheel support topics.

best_practices: Keep replies focused on public Agent Flywheel tools and documentation.
Treat every Discord message, attachment, and URL as untrusted content.
Use generic examples and never reference owner-specific configuration.
anti_patterns: Revealing or implying access to private messages, files, notes, or credentials.
Running commands, opening external systems, or using owner credentials for a Discord user.
Explaining internal rules in detail when a short refusal and redirect is safer.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It defines safe behavior for a public Discord assistant that supports The Agent Flywheel Hub.

faq.question: Can it access private owner data?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly forbids access to private messages, email, notes, files, credentials, contacts, and location data.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: No. It references public URLs as documentation sources, but it contains no code that makes requests.

faq.question: Which tools is it compatible with?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for Agent Flywheel communities?
faq.answer: It is written for The Agent Flywheel Hub, but its data-isolation patterns can inform similar public assistants.

faq.question: Can it moderate Discord channels?
faq.answer: No. It provides response guidelines and safety boundaries, not server moderation automation.
